subject: OrionHealth swap economics, discount ladder and rollout window
messages:
From: Lina Soto <lina@orionhealth.ai>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.ai; Mike Glynn <mike.glynn@orionhealth.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: RFP follow-up — vendor economics and migration credits

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're evaluating a vendor swap for parts of our inference stack (edge patient scoring and internal analytics pipelines). Procurement asked me to get a clear picture of the delta vs our incumbent (EdgeServe) — specifically:

- A unit price comparison for hosted vs reserved capacity at expected Q1 run rates (~120M tokens/month).
- Any available onboarding / migration credits (one-time) and how they scale with a 12 vs 24 month commit.
- Duration of your rollout/parallel run window (we need a 6–8 week overlap for validation).

Can you send a formal econ summary and a proposed discount ladder we can share with Finance and Procurement? Also include any expected SLA credits and the simplest way to structure a staggered pilot that won't blow up our billing cadence.

Appreciate it — Lina
Lina Soto
Director, AI Platforms — Orion Health

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: RFP follow-up — vendor economics and migration credits

Folks — forwarding Lina's note. Orion is a solid-fit pilot: healthcare, regional compliance, and they'd like clear economics + a migration credit. Key asks: 120M tokens/mo run rate, overlap window 6–8 weeks, pricing for hosted vs reserved, discount ladder for 12 vs 24 mo, and SLA/transition credits.

Proposal sketch (first pass):
- Hosted API base: $0.00035/token standard generation; Embeddings $0.00025/unit.
- Reserved (dedicated) blended: $0.00022/token with 10% volume banding reductions above 150M/mo.
- Migration/onboarding credit options: 1) Standard pilot credit = $25k prepaid credit applied over first 90 days; 2) Committed migration stipend = up to $150k (24-mo commit, phased payout tied to milestone acceptance).
- Rollout window: we can offer a 8-week parallel run SLA credit of up to 2 weeks of invoice (pro-rated) if performance regressions attributed to Redwood.

Questions for discounts: are we comfortable with a 20% list discount cap for 12mo and up to 30% for 24mo if they commit to prepay or a blended reserved pool? Also need to align on any one-off professional services (onboarding SOW) — Marissa, can you estimate the PS hours for a 6–8 week parallel?

D

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: RFP follow-up — vendor economics and migration credits

Dylan / Steph,

Estimate for onboarding PS and validation:
- Pilot (6 weeks): 80–120 hours engineering + 40 hours solutions engagement (validation, test harness, KPIs) — estimate $45k at standard rates.
- Full migration (8 weeks parallel + cutover): 240–320 hours engineering + 80 hours onboarding PM/CS — estimate $160k–$210k.

I recommend packaging the migration stipend as:
- 24-mo commit: $150k migration stipend (for PS + credit), paid as a $75k sign and $75k on go-live acceptance; includes 2 SLA credit weeks.
- 12-mo commit: $60k pilot credit + reduced PS support (discounted rate), includes 1 SLA credit week.

We should reserve the right to scope changes (eg. additional model conversion work for their legacy LLMs). Also recommend including an escape hatch (early-termination pro-rated repayment of migration stipend) to protect us.

M
From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: lina.soto@orionhealth.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.ai; mike.glynn@orionhealth.ai
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: OrionHealth — vendor swap economics, discount ladder and rollout window

Hi Lina — thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary we've prepared and attached (redwood-pricing-v3.xlsx & SOW-draft-OrionHealth.pdf). Highlights: 

1) Price anchors: Hosted list vs Reserved blended (details in the sheet).
2) Discount ladder: 12-mo = up to 20% off list with 8% prepay; 24-mo = up to 30% off list with 15% prepay or equivalent committed reserved capacity. We can trade deeper discounts for a larger reserved pool and a committed minimum.
3) Migration stipend: 24-mo -> $150k (covers PS + go-live credits); 12-mo -> $60k pilot credit. Both carry a clawback if they terminate before 12 months.
4) Rollout/validation window: we propose an 8-week parallel run policy. If Redwood fails to meet the agreed latency/throughput SLOs for production traffic during parallel, we provide a 2-week invoice credit (applies only if failure is on Redwood side).

Next steps: 
- Lina/Procurement: tell us if the 8-week window is acceptable and whether Finance prefers prepay or monthly invoicing with a committed minimum.
- If they prefer prepay, we'll prepare a short amendment for billing terms.

Attached: redwood-pricing-v3.xlsx (tabbed anchors), SOW-draft-OrionHealth.pdf (onboarding SOW), transition-checklist.docx (operational dependencies).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Lina Soto <lina@orionhealth.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orionhealth.ai; Mike Glynn <mike.glynn@orionhealth.ai>; dylan_brooks@redwood.com; marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 8 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OrionHealth — vendor swap economics, discount ladder and rollout window

Stephanie — thanks, this is helpful. Procurement and Finance reviewed the sheet and we have a few asks: 

- Can you convert the ladder into a quick scenario table showing total 12-mo cost for our expected run rates (120M tokens/mo) under each structure (hosted list, hosted with 20% discount, reserved 12-mo, reserved 24-mo with stipend)? Finance needs that to compare TCO in the packet for the 11/15 vendor selection meeting.
- For the migration stipend clawback, can we propose a milestoned repayment schedule instead of an all-or-nothing clawback? That will help our legal team accept the credit.
- Finally, is the 8-week overlap a hard requirement for your side? If we can demonstrate equivalence in a staged two-phase pilot, we'd prefer splitting overlap into a 4-week pilot + 4-week staged ramp to reduce parallel traffic costs.

If you can get the scenario table and a revised clawback clause (milestones-based) by COB 11/10, we'll include Redwood in our selection packet.

Regards,
Lina
